# LineChart

Line chart: one or more series over ordered categories, usually time. Use it for trends; for a single series
where the volume matters, AreaChart.

**Interaction**: a vertical crosshair follows the pointer and snaps to the nearest category; the tooltip lists
every visible series at that category, values first. `Tab` focuses the chart (focus ring only for the
keyboard); `←` / `→` move between categories with the same tooltip, `Home` / `End` jump to the first and last,
`Esc` hides the tooltip. Legend items show and hide series without changing colors; the "Chart / Table" switch
shows every value as a table.

**Category**: Charts · **Common uses**: Trends over time (revenue per month, active users per day), comparing a few series over the same period

## Import

```ts
import { LineChart } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

One series: the title says what is plotted, so there is no legend. Hover or focus the chart and use `←` / `→`
to read the values; the "Chart / Table" switch lists them all.

```tsx
export function Basic() {
  return (
    <LineChart
      title="Visits per month"
      description="January to August"
      data={months}
      x="month"
      xLabel="Month"
      series={[{ key: 'visits', name: 'Visits' }]}
    />
  )
}
```

## Variants

### Several series

From two series on, the legend appears; click an item to hide or show its series. Colors follow the position
in `series`, so the other series keep their colors.

```tsx
export function Series() {
  return (
    <LineChart
      title="Signups and trials"
      data={months}
      x="month"
      series={[
        { key: 'signups', name: 'Signups' },
        { key: 'trials', name: 'Trials' },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

### Emphasis

When the chart is about one series, `emphasis` keeps its color and mutes the others.

```tsx
export function Emphasis() {
  return (
    <LineChart
      title="Trials compared with the other funnels"
      data={months}
      x="month"
      emphasis="trials"
      series={[
        { key: 'signups', name: 'Signups' },
        { key: 'trials', name: 'Trials' },
        { key: 'visits', name: 'Visits' },
      ]}
      format="compact"
    />
  )
}
```

## States

### Loading, empty and error

The first load shows a delayed loading indicator at the height of the chart; reloading keeps the previous
lines at reduced opacity. Without rows the empty state is shown, and `error` with `onRetry` shows the error
state with "Retry".

```tsx
export function States() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <LineChart
        title="Visits per month"
        data={months}
        x="month"
        series={[{ key: 'visits', name: 'Visits' }]}
        loading={loading}
        actions={
          <Button size="small" onClick={() => setLoading((v) => !v)}>
            {loading ? 'Stop' : 'Reload'}
          </Button>
        }
      />
      <LineChart
        title="Visits per month"
        data={[]}
        x="month"
        series={[{ key: 'visits', name: 'Visits' }]}
        height={160}
      />
      <LineChart
        title="Visits per month"
        data={[]}
        x="month"
        series={[{ key: 'visits', name: 'Visits' }]}
        height={160}
        error="The analytics service did not respond."
        onRetry={() => {}}
      />
    </Stack>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `readonly T[]` | The rows: one per category (x), with a field per series. | — | Yes |
| `x` | `keyof T & string` | Field of the rows that holds the category (a text, a number or a date). | — | Yes |
| `series` | `readonly ChartSeries<keyof T & string>[]` | The series, in legend order. Colors follow the position in this array (or `slot`), so hiding or filtering a series never changes the color of the others. From the 9th series on, the muted color is used. | — | Yes |
| `format` | `ValueFormat` | How values are written on the value axis, in the tooltip and in the table. | `'auto'` | No |
| `xFormat` | `(value: ChartXValue) => string` | Writes a category, such as a date; by default `String(value)` (dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`). | — | No |
| `xLabel` | `string` | Name of the categories: the header of the first column of the table view. "Category" by default (follows `locale`). | — | No |
| `emphasis` | `keyof T & string` | Key of the one series the chart is about: it keeps its color and the others use the muted color. | — | No |
| `title` | `string` | Title of the chart: what is plotted. It is also the accessible name of the graphic. | — | No |
| `description` | `string` | A short description under the title, such as the period or the unit. | — | No |
| `height` | `number` | Height of the graphic in pixels, axis labels included. The states take the same height. The table view starts at this height and grows with its rows up to 480 px (or this height when it is taller); only longer tables scroll. | `240` | No |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Loading: without data, a delayed loading indicator takes the place of the graphic; with data, the previous graphic stays at reduced opacity until the new data arrives. | — | No |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | Error: `true` shows the default error state; a node is shown as the message of the error state. | — | No |
| `onRetry` | `() => void` | Retry after an error; shows a "Retry" button in the error state. | — | No |
| `emptyDescription` | `ReactNode` | Text of the empty state when there is no data, "No data" by default (follows `locale`). | — | No |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | Actions in the top-right corner, before the view switch (for example a menu or a time range). | — | No |
| `plain` | `boolean` | Without the card (no background, shadow or padding), for charts inside a Panel, a dialog or a drawer. | — | No |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
